meta.title: Operate Lightning Craft production through deployment-controller with Kata isolation
meta.author: manager

feature.problem_statement: Lightning Craft production is currently delivered by nested legacy Argo Application/ApplicationSet resources split between codicarium-prod and lc-prod-workload. This cannot be represented by deployment-controller's single grant/profile destination contract, leaves proxy and lobby outside the generated-server Kata policy, and has no verified dedicated LC Kata node pool on codicarium-prod.
goals: Make codicarium/lc-config the repository owner for every static LC production workload and policy.
Make deployment-controller the sole materializer for the LC production repository/environment.
Run proxy, lobby, and every generated Minecraft server with RuntimeClass kata-clh on dedicated LC nodes in codicarium-prod.
Prove the production stack is healthy and can create, reach, and retire a representative game server.
non_goals: Make individual dynamically created game-server instances Git-managed; the orchestrator remains their lifecycle owner.
Preserve the legacy split-cluster Application/ApplicationSet architecture or backwards-compatible delivery paths.
Schedule LC workloads on ARC runner nodes or weaken existing generated-server security controls.
scope_in: lc-config production descriptors, direct PathHelm charts, values, policies, tests, runbooks, and legacy-owner retirement.
codicarium/platform deployment-controller profile, grant, exposure classifications, resource allowlists, and activation evidence.
Codicarium prod infrastructure and platform GitOps needed for dedicated Kata-capable LC worker nodes and RuntimeClass kata-clh.
app-config removal of the legacy LC Argo owner after controller activation readiness is proven.
Production rollout, health checks, Minecraft proxy/lobby/generated-server smoke checks, rollback evidence, issue and PR lifecycle.
scope_out: Unrelated LC application features, service rewrites, and artifact migrations.
Live kubectl mutation as a deployment mechanism.
Reuse of ambiguous kubeconfig defaults or unnamed production contexts.

requirements.statement: The LC prod repository/environment MUST be materialized only by deployment-controller v0.13-compatible descriptors and one central DeploymentGrant/Profile after cutover; legacy nested Argo writers MUST be suppressed without overlapping ownership.
requirements.rationale: One authoritative reconciler prevents conflicting Applications and provides auditable, fail-closed activation.

requirements.statement: lc-config MUST directly own PathHelm-compatible production charts and values for orchestrator API, orchestrator worker, runtime policy/resources, database dependencies, proxy, and lobby, with explicit per-component exposureClass in central policy.
requirements.rationale: deployment-controller rejects repository attempts to define central authority and cannot materialize the current nested multi-source Application meta-chart unchanged.

requirements.statement: All static LC prod components and their runtime namespaces MUST target codicarium-prod under one destination profile; the separate lc-prod-workload destination MUST be retired from the LC prod delivery contract.
requirements.rationale: One grant references one profile and one destination; consolidating fulfills the requested Codicarium prod hosting model.

requirements.statement: RuntimeClass kata-clh MUST exist with a verified Kata handler and LC-specific scheduling constraints, and proxy, lobby, and all generated game-server Pods MUST set runtimeClassName kata-clh and schedule only on dedicated non-runner LC nodes.
requirements.rationale: Kata isolation must cover every player-facing server process without consuming or trusting ARC runner capacity.

requirements.statement: The consolidated prod stack MUST preserve least-privilege RBAC, generated-server admission, restricted pod security, image provenance, ExternalSecret-based credentials, persistent storage, network policy, public proxy routing, and internal service connectivity.
requirements.rationale: Changing the delivery and cluster boundary must not remove existing security or operational dependencies.

requirements.statement: Cutover MUST use deployment-controller prepare/activate evidence tied to the exact lc-config default-branch SHA, MUST avoid simultaneous legacy/controller ownership, and MUST provide a tested GitOps rollback that restores one known-good owner without deleting persistent data.
requirements.rationale: The production migration is high risk and controller activation is intentionally fail closed.

requirements.statement: Production validation MUST use an explicitly named codicarium-prod kube context and prove controller, Argo, nodes, RuntimeClass, storage, proxy, lobby, control-plane services, and a representative generated game-server lifecycle healthy.
requirements.rationale: Rendered desired state is not sufficient evidence that the player path is operational.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given merged controller policy and lc-config descriptor, when deployment-controller validates the prod repository, then every declared component ID/path matches one classified grant component, all rendered GVKs are allowlisted, and no legacy LC root/meta Application remains an active writer.

Given the prod render, when destinations and namespaces are inspected, then all static LC resources target codicarium-prod, no lc-prod-workload destination remains, and required RBAC, secrets, storage, network, and route resources render without plaintext secrets.

Given dedicated LC Kata nodes and RuntimeClass kata-clh, when proxy, lobby, and a generated game server are admitted, then each Pod declares kata-clh, lands on an LC node, cannot land on ARC runner nodes, and satisfies the generated-server security contract.

Given exact default-branch SHA and absent/conflict-free target Applications, when prepare and activate are executed through the controller workflow, then proof is accepted once, the controller owns all Applications, and rollback can restore the known-good Git owner without data deletion.

Given an explicitly named codicarium-prod context, when post-merge validation runs, then deployment-controller and Argo are healthy, all LC workloads are ready, a client reaches the public proxy and lobby, one generated server reaches ready and is reachable through the proxy, and cleanup/stop completes successfully.

test_plan.approach: Strictly decode both prod descriptor and central grant/profile using deployment-controller v0.13.0 contracts; assert exact component/path/value/exposure mappings and rejection of unknown or missing fields.

Run Helm lint/template for every local component chart and assert one codicarium-prod destination, exact namespaces, required GVK allowlist, no nested Applications, no plaintext secrets, and expected storage/network/RBAC resources.

Render and server-side dry-run RuntimeClass, proxy, lobby, and generated-server fixtures; positive kata-clh cases pass while missing/wrong runtime, unsafe security settings, wrong node placement, mutable images, and runner-node placement fail closed.
Exercise controller dry-run/prepare/activate checks and a documented rollback rehearsal using exact immutable SHAs and conflict detection before production activation.
With explicit prod kubeconfig/context, verify nodes/controllers/Argo/workloads/storage and run the public proxy to lobby to generated-server lifecycle smoke test, collecting non-secret evidence.

review_checks: Verify exactly one materializer and no nested/overlapping Argo ownership.
validation_checks: Controller activation evidence and Application ownership are exact-SHA bound.

review_checks: Verify direct local charts, central authority fields, and every component classification.
validation_checks: All controller descriptor/grant mappings and Helm renders pass.

review_checks: Verify removal of lc-prod-workload destination references from active prod delivery.
validation_checks: All static LC workloads observed in codicarium-prod only.

review_checks: Verify handler, overhead/scheduling, LC node isolation, and all three workload paths.
validation_checks: Proxy, lobby, and generated server report kata-clh and LC-node placement.

review_checks: Review RBAC, admission, secrets, images, storage, networking, and public exposure least privilege.
validation_checks: Negative policy tests fail and dependency health checks pass.

review_checks: Verify conflict-free activation ordering and persistent-data-safe rollback.
validation_checks: Prepare/activate and rollback rehearsal evidence accepted.

review_checks: Verify commands pin kubeconfig and codicarium-prod context and expose no secrets.
validation_checks: End-to-end player path and generated-server cleanup pass live.

perspectives.summary: Use a staged four-repository cutover: substrate, controller policy, lc-config direct charts/descriptor, then legacy-owner suppression and activation.
One grant/profile cannot preserve the current two destinations. Consolidate into codicarium-prod and require exact resource allowlists and exposure classes.
Keep Kata on dedicated LC nodes, retain fail-closed generated-server admission, ExternalSecrets, restricted pods, and prevent ARC runner placement.
Require offline render/contract negatives, controller activation proof, explicit-context live checks, and a player-path lifecycle smoke test before completion.

council.consensus_summary: Proceed with desired-state implementation and PRs. Production activation is NO-GO until a dedicated Kata-capable LC node pool exists and an explicitly named codicarium-prod kube context passes preflight.
open_questions: The exact Kata containerd handler and RuntimeClass overhead must be derived from the pinned platform chart and proven on the dedicated LC node pool before activation.
